header.title: Select
header.description: Single-select dropdown with composable option children

children.content:
## Import

```tsx
import { Input } from "@toni-toni-choppa/ui-kit";
```

---

## Example

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Input } from "@toni-toni-choppa/ui-kit";

export default function SelectExample() {
	const [role, setRole] = useState("developer");

	return (
		<Input.Select id="role" onChange={setRole}>
			<Input.Select.Option value="developer" label="Developer" />
			<Input.Select.Option value="designer" label="Designer" />
			<Input.Select.Option value="manager" label="Manager" />
		</Input.Select>
	);
}
```

---

## Props

### `Input.Select`

- `id: string` (required): `id` for the underlying `<select>` element.
- `children: React.ReactNode` (required): one or more `Input.Select.Option` elements.
- `onChange?: (value: string) => void`: callback with the selected option value.
- `disabled?: boolean`: disables interaction.
- `className?: string`: optional class for the outer wrapper.

### `Input.Select.Option`

- `value: string` (required): option value.
- `label: string` (required): visible option text.
- `className?: string`: optional class for the option.

---

## Notes

- `Input.Select` uses a custom wrapper with a built-in dropdown icon.
- The selected value is controlled by the browser unless you manage state externally in `onChange`.

index.content:
## Overview This UI Kit provides reusable React components for building forms and documentation-style layouts. Currently available public components: - `Button` - `Article` - `Input` (`Text`, `Select`, `TextArea`, `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `Range`) --- ## Installation Install the package with your preferred package manager. ### Requirements - React 18+ - A bundler that supports CSS modules (Vite, Next.js, CRA, etc.) ### Install ```bash npm install @toni-toni-choppa/ui-kit ``` --- ## Basic Usage ```tsx import { Button, Input } from "@toni-toni-choppa/ui-kit"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` --- ## Component Docs - Start with the `Input` module for all form controls. - Use `Button` for primary and secondary actions. - Use `Article` to structure long-form content sections.
